claims.text: Optimized annealing protocols can increase the coercive field of magnetic high-entropy alloys relative to an as-cast or conventionally annealed baseline.
Optimized annealing alters the microstructure and phase constitution of magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Annealing-induced beneficial phase transformations are the mechanism expected to increase coercivity.
The predicted coercivity increase should hold at room temperature under standard magnetic testing protocols.
The proposed effect is limited to magnetic high-entropy alloy compositions that can undergo annealing-driven phase transformations.
The extent of the coercivity increase and the optimal annealing parameters are uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing annealed samples with matched as-cast or conventionally annealed controls.
Failure to observe a statistically significant coercive-field increase relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
